title: Email: Fw: The truth about the Kirk Gibson picture

content.subject: Fw: The truth about the Kirk Gibson picture

content.text:
Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: GEORGE BEAVER <georgebeaver@sbcglobal.net>
Sent: Sunday, April 19, 2020 8:54 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: The truth about the Kirk Gibson picture 
 
Hello Anthony,

So to start Mary Scroeder take the picture but, the picture did have some help from the guys in the art department.  My uncle work at the Free Press for years as a cartoonist and illustrator.  His name was Leroy Beaver.  He worker under Dick Mayer back in the day.  Anyways back in "84" he was still hard at work in the art department.  I stop down that week of the photo just for a visit.  He was my favorite uncle.  After we started talking about this and that he brought up the picture to my surprise.  He was very very modest and shy.  He and said Mary had taken the picture and brought it back to the paper to print.  After some discussion with another person in the art department.  He decided to cut out Kirk Gibson with a X-acto knife and wash out the back with the crowd and stadium.  The he pasted the picture of Kirk over the wash out back to make it look 3-d.  The rest is history they say.  That was the first time that he did that and was very proud.  He did a few more iconic pictures for the sports department like that.  Ask some of the old timers down at the paper if they remember Leroy Beaver.  Thanks any questions please feel free to call.
George Beaver  586-883-4036
